what: resolveId's raw-hash tolerance — an old account hash accepted where a pubid is now the wire id
pattern: SELECT hash FROM profiles WHERE hash = \?1 LIMIT 1'\)\.bind\(wire\)
how: once every shared `profile.html?u=<hash>` link and push `?dm=<hash>` URL minted before the L3 flip has aged out (30 days), drop resolveId's trailing raw-hash lookup so only a pubid resolves; an account hash on the wire is then simply unknown.

what: weakKeyTolerated — a WEAK identity key that already has history behind it may still write
how: delete weakKeyTolerated() and the `known && weakKeyTolerated()` clause in keyFloor, so the floor holds for EVERY write. A weak-key member is no longer locked out: key rotation (POST /profile/rekey, 2026-09-18) lets them move to a strong key with their content, so on the due date a weak key is refused a write and told to rotate. Run scripts/key_audit.py first and give any cracked member a heads-up to rotate; move this date only if one cannot be reached in time.

what: the legacy actor_hash clause: a DM bell from before 0016 named its sender, not its thread
how: once no unread bell with topic_id 0 remains, drop this clause and the two `topic_id = 0 AND actor_hash` clauses in routes/dm.ts; tests/worker/notif_read
